findings.explanation: The new GET /orders/<order_id> endpoint (get_order) fetches an Order by a user-controlled order_id and returns order.to_dict() with only @require_auth, which merely authenticates and sets g.current_user (app/auth.py:55-66) — it performs no ownership or role check. Policy §3 mandates: 'Every endpoint that fetches an order by its identifier MUST verify ownership with is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id) before returning data.' The helper is_owner_or_admin is imported in orders.py (line 13) but never called in get_order, so any authenticated user can read any other user's order (including shipping_address, total, status). This is an IDOR. The reference pattern in users.py get_user (lines 28-38) correctly applies is_owner_or_admin and returns 403, confirming the intended control that is missing here.

evidence.content:
## 3. Order data access rules

- A user may view ONLY their own orders. Every endpoint that fetches an order by its identifier MUST verify ownership with `is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id)` before returning data.

findings.suggested_fix: In get_order, after resolving the order, enforce ownership before returning data: `if not is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, order.user_id): return jsonify({"error": "forbidden"}), 403`. This matches the get_user reference pattern and policy §3.
